body:
Found the culprit: 85ae1905d4abfcd214bd53d6cd3d032ff246daf6, which is a rollback of c4134802dd15d6ef5cca6521f6bf6aac395ee2ad, which itself is a rollback of 1d9e1ac90197b1d3d7b137ba3c1ada67bb9ba31b.

I have an empty WORKSPACE file in a directory.

Pre-culprit:
```
  $ ../../gitroot/bazel/bazel-bin/src/bazel --batch info bazel-bin
Extracting Bazel installation...
(14:44:19) INFO: Current date is 2017-05-31
(...)/execroot/github3055/bazel-out/local-fastbuild/bin
```

At culprit:
```
  $ ../../gitroot/bazel/bazel-bin/src/bazel --batch info bazel-bin
Extracting Bazel installation...
(14:46:45) INFO: Current date is 2017-05-31
(...)/execroot/__main__/bazel-out/local-fastbuild/bin
```
So as I understand it, this is now working as intended. @kchodorow , can you confirm?

The problem does now seem to be specific to workspaces without an explicitly-specified name.

Just built bazel from HEAD, and in the case where it falls back to the default workspace name, no symlink directory is set up in execroot/, which contains only '__main__' (however `execution_root` in `bazel info` still points to execroot/[root_dir_name], which doesn't exist).

Unfortunately `bazel info` it not able to pick up the "correct" workspace name yet (the workspace name is discovered during the build's loading phase and `info` never gets there).  I think this is a bug, we shouldn't be returning a non-existent dir, it might actually be better just to make this return `<output_base>/execroot` (with no directory suffix), as I think that's the direction we're moving (@lberki has proposed making actions cd to execroot, not `execroot/ws`, before running).

body:
If I build bazel from HEAD now, this appears to have regressed a little since the initial report -- for workspaces with non-default names, the 'execution_root' shown by bazel info exists, but is empty (it's no longer a symlink to the actual exec root).

bazel-bin, bazel-genfiles, etc. point to directories which actually exist, underneath the actual exec root.

This is breaking IntelliJ support, because we rely on knowing the execution root (e.g. to decode execution root relative paths).
Marking as a release blocker unless someone says otherwise.
